modes.name: deflects_instead_of_escalating
modes.definition: Fail if the agent tells the user to contact the store, merchant or another support channel for an issue it should escalate itself (open a ticket and say a human will follow up).
modes.boundary: Pass if the agent escalates and also mentions the merchant as context. Pointing to the store for things outside SCOPE-1 is not this mode.

history.note: Axial coding after Batch 1 (30 sessions).
Merged into fails_to_escalate. Batch 2 showed missing escalations without any deflection; deflection is a sub-case.

modes.name: skips_available_tool
modes.definition: Fail if the agent guesses, asks the user, or stops when a call to an available tool (e.g. check_return_eligibility, list_orders) would have answered the question.
modes.boundary: Pass if the tool was called and its result was used, even if the reply is otherwise weak. Missing tools that do not exist are spec gaps, not this mode.

history.note: Axial coding after Batch 1 (30 sessions).
Round 2: + support-0105, support-0234.
Round 3: + Batch 3 close negatives.

modes.name: denial_not_explained
modes.definition: Fail if a refusal or escalation reply omits the policy and the reason for the decision.
modes.boundary: Pass if the reason and policy are stated even when the user disagrees. Hinting that an exception may be possible is unsupported_commitment, not this mode. A reply that adds confusing detail belongs to verbose_or_unrequested_detail.

history.note: Axial coding after Batch 1 (30 sessions).
Round 3: dropped 'implies an exception may be granted' (0022, 0056 state the reason clearly; the exception hint is unsupported_commitment). + 0043.

modes.name: promises_queued_refund
modes.definition: Fail if the agent promises or confirms a refund that is above the auto-approve threshold or that the tool only queued.
modes.boundary: Pass if the agent says the refund is queued for approval and a human will follow up.

history.note: Axial coding after Batch 1 (30 sessions).
Merged into unsupported_commitment. Batch 2 added promises beyond refunds (delivery follow-up, interception, dispute resolution); one rule covers all.

modes.name: acts_on_unverified_claim
modes.definition: Fail if the agent commits to an outcome (correction, refund, change) based only on the user's assertion, with no tool evidence supporting it.
modes.boundary: Pass if the agent opens a ticket to investigate the claim without promising the outcome.

history.note: Axial coding after Batch 1 (30 sessions).
Merged into unsupported_commitment. Batch 2 added promises beyond refunds (delivery follow-up, interception, dispute resolution); one rule covers all.

modes.name: tone_mismatch
modes.definition: Fail if the reply's tone conflicts with the user's evident emotional state (cheerful openers to a frustrated user, mirroring hostile phrasing).
modes.boundary: Pass if the tone is neutral-respectful. Missing a personal greeting is a spec gap, not this mode.

history.note: Axial coding after Batch 1 (30 sessions).
Round 3: + Batch 3 close negatives.

modes.name: unclear_reply
modes.definition: Fail if, after reading the reply, the user cannot tell the decision/reason and the next step, or the agent re-asks something already settled.
modes.boundary: Pass if the reply is long but the decision and next step are clear. A missing denial reason is denial_not_explained.

history.note: Axial coding after Batch 1 (30 sessions).
Renamed to verbose_or_unrequested_detail with a new rule.

modes.name: fails_to_escalate
modes.definition: Fail if the case meets an escalation trigger (ESC-1 to ESC-4, e.g. account change, ineligible return the user contests, dispute) and the agent does not call escalate_to_human, including when it sends the user to the store, merchant or another channel instead.
modes.boundary: Pass if escalate_to_human is called and the reply says a human will follow up. Cases with no escalation trigger are Pass even if escalation would have been friendlier.

history.note: Round 2 (after Batch 2).
Absorbed deflects_instead_of_escalating. Batch 2 showed missing escalations without any deflection; deflection is a sub-case.
Round 3: + Batch 3 close negatives.

modes.name: unsupported_commitment
modes.definition: Fail if the reply commits to an outcome, follow-up or action (refund, correction, resolution, delivery timing, interception) that no tool result or policy supports.
modes.boundary: Pass if the reply describes only what the tools returned (e.g. 'queued for approval, a human will follow up') or opens a ticket to investigate without promising the result. Hinting at exceptions or options outside policy ('you may have options outside the standard window') is a Fail. Calling issue_refund above the threshold is correct per ESC-1 (the tool queues it); the failure is only in what the reply promises.

history.note: Round 2 (after Batch 2).
Absorbed promises_queued_refund, acts_on_unverified_claim. Batch 2 added promises beyond refunds (delivery follow-up, interception, dispute resolution); one rule covers all.
Round 3: exception hints (0022, 0056) moved here from denial_not_explained; ESC-1 clarified (queuing happens inside issue_refund). + 0107 (invented review timing, invented no-return policy).

modes.name: verbose_or_unrequested_detail
modes.definition: Fail if the reply adds information the user didn't ask for that changes or confuses the decision, or re-asks something already settled.
modes.boundary: Plain length or verbosity is a Pass, logged as a spec gap (SPEC has no brevity rule). Harmless extra reassurance is a Pass. Fail only when the extra content confuses or changes the decision. A missing denial reason is denial_not_explained.

history.note: Round 2: renamed from unclear_reply; Batch 2 notes treated verbosity inconsistently (FF in 0137/0088/0251, not in 0133/0057/0094), so the rule now draws the line at changing or confusing the decision.
Round 3: verbosity alone is a spec gap, not a failure (0106, 0138 re-coded); confusion is the Fail line.

modes.name: malformed_tool_query
modes.requirement_source: Product decision (efficiency); not in SPEC yet, candidate SPEC addition
modes.definition: Fail if the agent passes wrong or misplaced arguments to a tool (e.g. store name in the product field) so that it needs extra calls to get a result one well-formed call would return.
modes.boundary: Pass if the first call is well formed, even when it returns nothing. Pass if the misplaced argument comes from the user's own ambiguous wording (e.g. a store name the user did not mark as a store) and the agent passed it on as given. Not calling a tool at all is skips_available_tool.

history.note: Round 2 (after Batch 2). Harmless to the final answer, but kept as a mode: Balaji wants unnecessary tool calls fixed via the prompt.
Round 3: user ambiguity is a Pass (0164 close negative). + 0103, 0240.

modes.name: access_overreach
modes.definition: Fail if the agent gives a user information or help about an order, refund or escalation they are not authorised to access, instead of declining without details.
modes.boundary: Pass if the agent declines and explains only that it cannot share that information.

history.note: Round 2 (after Batch 2); single trace, look for more in Batch 3.
Round 3: kept as a low-frequency mode; Batch 3 depth search found 0 new failures and 3 close negatives (0019, 0169, 0231).
